Hi all — quick operational confirmation and an example so Marjorie's team can model the numbers. TL;DR: default is prospective degression; channel commission is a post-discount line item by default, but we can offer a pre-discount flow for larger commitments. Details: 

1) Degression handling:
- Default: prospective only. Example: SKU threshold = 100k token-hours. If Month M and M+1 exceed threshold, degression rate applies starting Month M+2. No retroactive credit.
- Exception: we can grant retrospective adjustment back to Month M if Legal/Finance approves (we treat as a credit on the next invoice). That requires a signed amendment in DocuSign and will adjust revenue recognition.

2) Channel crediting flow (default):
- List price (line A)
- Private-offer discount applied -> Net customer price (line B)
- Distributor commission computed as percentage of line B and shown as separate line (line C)
- Net collected = line B - line C

Example (numbers):
- List price per month (SKU X): $100,000
- Private-offer discount: 30% -> Net customer price: $70,000
- Distributor commission: 15% of $70,000 = $10,500 -> shown as distributor credit line
- Redwood collects $59,500

If DataOps needs commission taken from list price (pre-discount), we can support that but we'll need to: 
- Update the billing spec (ops change)
- Update the private-offer term sheet to call out pre-discount passback
- Confirm any tax implications with Finance

I've attached the term sheet v2 with the billing options section highlighted — if you want the pre-discount option, mark it and we'll route to Legal/Finance for amendment.
